description: Captures a whole web page and writes it to disk. Name a tabId from list_tabs to capture a tab that is already open, a url to open one and capture that, or urls to capture a list of pages one after another. A PDF keeps real, selectable text; PNG and JPEG are images. Returns the absolute path it wrote, and a truncated report when the page was too large to capture whole; for urls, one result per page, each with its path or its error. Set markdown to get the page as text too, which is far easier to read than a PDF. A tall page or a long list can take minutes. When the answer has status "running", the capture is still going in the browser: call this tool again with exactly the same arguments to wait for its result, and do not start another capture of that tab meanwhile.

accessibility.description: Also check the page against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 (levels A and AA) with axe-core, and write two files beside the capture: <name>.accessibility.pdf, the page with each failing element boxed and numbered and the rules listed after it, and <name>.accessibility.json, every rule and element with its box on the page in CSS px. The result has accessibility{pdfPath, reportPath, elements, passed, byImpact, rules[]}, or null when the check could not run on the page. An automated check finds some of what fails WCAG, not all of it: say so when reporting that nothing failed.

browserId.description: Which browser to act on, from list_browsers. Optional when only one is connected. Chrome runs a separate extension per profile, so a work profile and a personal profile are two different browsers.

captureWidth.description: Lay the page out at the width of a sheet before capturing it, the way a narrow window would, so the PDF prints at 1:1. "window" (the default) takes the page at the width the browser has it; "a4" and "letter" reflow it. A 1280 px window on A4 is scaled to 55 %, which puts 16 px body text at 6.5 pt; "a4" puts it at 12.

colorScheme.description: Which of a page's two themes to capture. "auto" (the default) is whatever the browser is set to; "light" and "dark" force one. A page with only one version is unchanged.

fileName.description: The file name inside outputPath, as a template: {n}, {host}, {name}, {date}, {time}, {ext}. {n} is the page's place in urls, {host} its host, {name} the name the browser suggests, {date} and {time} when the call started; {ext} is added when left out, and a / makes a subdirectory.

hide.description: Clutter to hide before the capture and put back after: ads, consent (cookie banners), chat (chat widgets), overlays (modals, their backdrop, "open in the app" bars). [] hides nothing. Left out, the extension's own settings decide. The result counts what was hidden as "hidden". Leave the page whole when the user wants a record of how it looked.

highlight.description: Passages you quoted from this page, to highlight in the file where the page has them as written, the way check_quotes finds them; a PDF lists each under a "Quoted passages" bookmark. Give the exact words you quoted, after check_quotes found them. The result says which were found as highlighted[]; one not found is not marked. One page only: not with urls.

markdown.description: The page as Markdown, read from the page itself rather than from the PDF: "inline" returns the text in this result, "beside" writes a .md next to the file, "only" writes the .md and no file. Each also returns the page's title, address, capture time, language and headings as "page". Pictures are left out of the text.

openEditor.description: Leave the capture open in a Page Scanner editor tab as well.

outputPath.description: Where to write the file. A directory keeps the suggested filename, and a leading ~ is the home directory. Defaults to the working directory, or to ~/Downloads when that is the filesystem root or cannot be written, as under Claude Desktop.

pageSize.description: PDF only. "a4" and "letter" slice the capture onto printable sheets with a half-inch margin; "auto" is one page the exact size of the capture, which is not printable and which Acrobat clamps past 200 inches.

pictureFiles.description: Also write the page's pictures and canvases (charts, diagrams, screenshots, at least 120 by 40 px), cut from the capture where they were drawn, as PNGs in a folder beside the file. The result lists pictures[] with each path, kind and box. They are what the page showed, not the files it loaded.

slices.description: Also write the page as PNG slices, top to bottom, for looking at it with a vision model: true for slices of at most 1568 px a side (past which Claude shrinks a picture), or a side in pixels (256 to 4096) for another model. A whole-page screenshot of a long page is shrunk until its text is unreadable; a slice is not. Each slice repeats the last lines of the one before. The result lists slices[].path with the band of the page (y, height, in CSS px) each shows, in a folder beside the file; open them to look at the page.

tabId.description: A tab from list_tabs. Give one of tabId, url or urls.

tables.description: The page's tables as rows of cell text, for reading a table as data rather than from the Markdown or the PDF: "inline" returns them in this result as tables.tables[], "beside" writes <name>.tables.json next to the file. Each has rows (every row as wide as the widest, a cell's words on one line, an icon by its name), header (the first row is the page's header) and box (where it was on the page, in CSS px); tables.sizes gives each one's rows and columns. A <table>, an ARIA table and a CSS grid drawn as a table all count; a virtualized grid has only the rows it had drawn. With markdown, textOptions.scope and redact apply to them as to the text.

textOptions.description: How the markdown is written, to fit it in a context window; only with markdown. Every heading in page.headings has offset and chars, a map of the text's sections.

links.description: "references" writes [words][n] and lists each address once at the end; "text" keeps the words and drops the addresses. Default "inline".

maxChars.description: At most this many characters after the front matter, kept in whole blocks. page.cut then says how long the whole text was and how many blocks were left out.

pictures.description: "alt" leaves [Picture: alt text] where a picture was. Default "omit".

redact.description: Replace every email address, phone number, card and IBAN, ID or tax number, IP address, key and token that Sensitive Text's rules find, and the user's own patterns, with a numbered placeholder such as ⟦EMAIL 1⟧ before the text leaves the browser; the same value is the same placeholder. Use it for a signed-in page whose text goes to a cloud model. Only the Markdown, and the tables with it, are redacted, not a PDF or picture written with it, so pair it with markdown "inline" or "only". page.redacted counts what was replaced, never the values.

scope.description: "main" writes only the main content the extension found (an article, the docs column), leaving out navigation, sidebars and footers; the whole page when it found none, and page.scope says which.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long the browser may take over one page, in seconds. Default 120. A very tall page, such as a long chat or feed, can take longer. Not how long this call waits: a capture that outlasts the call keeps going (see the tool description).

url.description: Opens a background tab on this address, captures it, and closes it again. Give one of tabId, url or urls.

urls.description: Several addresses, up to 50, captured one at a time into outputPath, which is then a directory. A page that fails is reported and the next one captured. Give one of tabId, url or urls.

videoHandling.description: What to do with a video: keep its paused frame, or leave the area blank.

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for a browser to connect, in seconds. Chrome retires the extension after about thirty seconds of silence, so the default covers the reconnect. 0 fails immediately.

windowId.description: Which window to open `url` in, from list_tabs. Ignored when tabId is given.

name: scan_page
title: Capture a page to a file
